notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Isaiah 47 this time, because I wasn't able to read a single source page.

My first attempt tried to fetch eight pages at once: Enduring Word, the Ellicott, Pulpit, Gill, Barnes and Jamieson-Fausset-Brown commentaries on biblehub.com, preceptaustin.org and netbible.org. That went over the tool's usage limit and returned nothing. When I tried again with just the Enduring Word page, the tool had no calls left for this turn.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. Since I have no page content, anything I wrote would come from memory, so I've left the notes empty rather than fill them myself.

If you ask again, I'll read the sources one or two at a time to stay under the limit, in this order:
1. **The traditional reading:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-47/, then the Ellicott, Pulpit, Gill and Barnes pages on biblehub.com, then preceptaustin.org.
2. **Modern scholarship:** the netbible.org notes on Isaiah 47.
3. **Differences between traditions and other views:** searches on the tradition-specific sites. Likely verses are vv. 8 and 10 (Babylon saying "I am, and there is none besides me," compared with God's own words and often linked to Revelation 18) and vv. 12–14 (sorcery and astrology).
